title: EU & UK -- anti-money-laundering basics
description: Plain-language anti-money-laundering (AML) and sanctions obligations for regulated financial services firms in the EU and UK: customer due diligence, sanctions screening, politically exposed persons, suspicious activity reporting, and record keeping.
disclaimer: Decision support only, not legal advice. AML requirements vary by country and firm type; confirm them with your MLRO or compliance team.

regulations.name: Anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing rules (EU AML directives, UK Money Laundering Regulations)
regulations.summary: Customer due diligence, monitoring, reporting, and record-keeping duties for regulated firms.

obligations.title: Identify and verify customers before establishing a relationship
obligations.text: Customer due diligence (identifying the customer and any beneficial owner, and verifying their identity) must be completed before a business relationship is established or a transaction carried out.

controls.title: Onboarding cannot complete until identity is verified
controls.description: An onboarding flow blocks activation until identity verification has passed; failures or mismatches go to a person.

obligations.title: Screen customers and payments against sanctions lists
obligations.text: Customers and relevant transactions must be screened against applicable sanctions lists. Potential matches must be investigated before proceeding and must not be resolved automatically.

controls.title: Potential sanctions matches are reviewed by a person
controls.description: Any potential sanctions match stops the process and is escalated to the MLRO or a nominated compliance officer for review; it is never cleared automatically.

obligations.title: Apply enhanced due diligence to politically exposed persons
obligations.text: Where a customer is a politically exposed person (PEP), enhanced due diligence applies, including senior management approval for the relationship and establishing the source of wealth and funds.

controls.title: PEP relationships need senior management approval
controls.description: A customer flagged as a PEP cannot be onboarded without approval from senior management.

obligations.title: Report suspicious activity internally to the MLRO
obligations.text: Staff and systems must report knowledge or suspicion of money laundering to the money laundering reporting officer (MLRO), who decides whether to report externally. The customer must not be tipped off.

controls.title: Suspicious activity is escalated to the MLRO without telling the customer
controls.description: Automated steps that detect suspicious patterns escalate to the MLRO and must not disclose the escalation in any customer communication.

obligations.title: Keep due diligence and transaction records for five years
obligations.text: Records of customer due diligence and of transactions must be kept for at least five years after the end of the relationship or the transaction.

controls.title: Retain due diligence evidence for five years
controls.description: Evidence gathered by the process (documents checked, screening results, decisions) is stored with a retention period of at least five years.

glossary.definition: Money laundering reporting officer: the person responsible for receiving internal suspicious activity reports and deciding whether to report externally.
Politically exposed person: someone entrusted with a prominent public function, or their close family or associates.
Customer due diligence: identifying and verifying a customer and understanding the purpose of the relationship.
